question: What is the product of: $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{ONa} + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{I} \rightarrow$?
explanation: Allyloxide displaces iodide from ethyl iodide via $S_N2$ to produce allyl ethyl ether.
subject: Chemistry

question: Why does reaction of sodium ethoxide with bromocyclohexane give predominantly cyclohexene?
options: Bromocyclohexane is a secondary halide and undergoes $E2$ elimination readily with the strong base ethoxide
explanation: Secondary halides undergo facile anti-periplanar $E2$ elimination with strong bases, giving the cycloalkene as the major product.
subject: Chemistry

question: Identify reagent $X$ in: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow{X} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{O}^-\text{Na}^+$:
explanation: Alcohols are weaker acids than water, so strong bases like $\text{Na}$ metal or $\text{NaH}$ are needed for complete conversion to alkoxide.
subject: Chemistry

question: What is the product of intramolecular displacement in 5-bromopentan-1-ol with base?
explanation: Deprotonation of the terminal hydroxyl group generates an alkoxide that attacks C-5, expelling bromide to close a stable 6-membered tetrahydropyran ring.
subject: Chemistry

question: Which of the following ethers CANNOT be synthesized by Williamson method?
explanation: Di-tert-butyl ether requires reaction of a tertiary halide with a tertiary alkoxide, which results exclusively in $E2$ elimination to 2-methylpropene.
subject: Chemistry

question: What are the reagents used in the Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) Reaction?
options: Carboxylic acid with chlorine ($\text{Cl}_2$) or bromine ($\text{Br}_2$) in the presence of a catalytic amount of red phosphorus ($\text{P}_{\text{red}}$), followed by water hydrolysis
Carboxylic acid with thionyl chloride only
Carboxylic acid with nitric acid and sulfuric acid
explanation: The HVZ reaction selectively halogenates the $\alpha$-position of aliphatic carboxylic acids using halogen ($\text{Br}_2$ or $\text{Cl}_2$) and catalytic red phosphorus.
subject: Chemistry

question: What is the major product of the HVZ reaction of acetic acid with bromine and red phosphorus?
explanation: Bromination occurs exclusively at the $\alpha$-carbon of acetic acid to yield $\alpha$-bromoacetic acid (bromoacetic acid).
subject: Chemistry

question: Which essential structural feature MUST a carboxylic acid possess to undergo the HVZ reaction?
options: At least one $\alpha$-hydrogen atom on the carbon adjacent to the carboxyl group
explanation: The reaction mechanism proceeds via an enol intermediate involving the $\alpha$-carbon; without an $\alpha$-hydrogen, enolization cannot occur and the reaction fails.
subject: Chemistry

question: Which of the following carboxylic acids CANNOT undergo the Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction?
options: Trimethylacetic acid (Pivalic acid, $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-COOH}$) and Benzoic acid
explanation: Pivalic acid ($(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-COOH}$) and benzoic acid ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOH}$) have no $\alpha$-hydrogens and cannot undergo $\alpha$-halogenation.
subject: Chemistry

question: What is the catalytic role of red phosphorus in the HVZ reaction?
options: It reacts in situ with halogen to form phosphorus trihalide ($\text{PBr}_3$ or $\text{PCl}_3$), which converts a portion of the acid into the more easily enolizable acyl halide
It acts as a reducing agent to remove oxygen
It absorbs water to dry the solvent
explanation: Free carboxylic acids enolize very poorly. $\text{PBr}_3$ converts the acid into acyl bromide ($R\text{CH}_2\text{COBr}$), which enolizes rapidly into an enol that reacts with bromine.
subject: Chemistry

question: What is the reactive enol intermediate formed during the HVZ bromination of propanoic acid?
explanation: Propanoyl bromide tautomerizes to its enol form, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{C(OH)Br}$, whose nucleophilic $\alpha$-carbon attacks molecular bromine.
subject: Chemistry

question: How is the $\alpha$-bromo acyl bromide converted to the final $\alpha$-bromo carboxylic acid in the catalytic cycle?
options: By exchange with an unreacted molecule of carboxylic acid ($R\text{CH(Br)COBr} + R\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} \rightleftharpoons R\text{CH(Br)COOH} + R\text{CH}_2\text{COBr}$) or by aqueous work-up
explanation: The $\alpha$-halo acyl bromide undergoes exchange with another molecule of carboxylic acid, regenerating the acyl bromide catalyst and liberating the $\alpha$-halo acid.
subject: Chemistry

question: Why cannot iodine or fluorine be used effectively in the standard HVZ reaction?
options: Because iodine is an acid and fluorine is a base
Fluorine reacts violently and uncontrollably causing extensive decomposition, while iodination is thermodynamically unfavorable and reversible
explanation: Fluorination is excessively exothermic and non-selective; iodination is endothermic with unfavorable equilibrium. Only chlorine and bromine work well.
subject: Chemistry

question: What is the product when propanoic acid is treated with excess bromine and red phosphorus?
explanation: With excess halogen and prolonged reaction times, both $\alpha$-hydrogens on the methylene carbon are sequentially replaced, yielding 2,2-dibromopropanoic acid.
subject: Chemistry

question: What synthetic transformation occurs when an $\alpha$-bromo carboxylic acid is treated with excess aqueous ammonia?
options: Reduction back to the carboxylic acid
explanation: Nucleophilic substitution of the $\alpha$-bromine by ammonia yields $\alpha$-amino acids (e.g., converting propanoic acid via 2-bromopropanoic acid to DL-alanine).
subject: Chemistry

question: How can an $\alpha$-halo acid be converted into an $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated carboxylic acid?
options: By dehydrohalogenation using alcoholic $\text{KOH}$ or a hindered base (e.g., $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(Br)COOH} \xrightarrow{\text{alc. KOH}} \text{CH}_2=\text{CH-COOH}$)
explanation: Elimination of hydrogen halide ($E2$) from the $\alpha$-halo acid using alcoholic base creates an $\alpha,\beta$-double bond, yielding acrylic or crotonic acids.
subject: Chemistry

question: What is the product when an $\alpha$-bromo acid is treated with warm aqueous $\text{KOH}$?
explanation: Aqueous $\text{KOH}$ promotes nucleophilic substitution ($S_N2$) of the bromide by hydroxide, yielding $\alpha$-hydroxy carboxylic acids (e.g. lactic acid from 2-bromopropanoic acid).
subject: Chemistry

question: What is the product when phenylacetic acid ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$) is subjected to the HVZ reaction?
explanation: The benzylic $\alpha$-carbon has two acidic hydrogens and undergoes selective halogenation, giving $\alpha$-bromophenylacetic acid.
subject: Chemistry

question: Why does formic acid ($\text{HCOOH}$) NOT give the HVZ reaction?
options: It is not a carboxylic acid
It has no $\alpha$-carbon atom (the hydrogen is attached directly to the carbonyl carbon)
It is a gas at room temperature
explanation: Formic acid possesses only a formyl hydrogen and lacks an $\alpha$-carbon, making enolization impossible; halogen oxidizes it to $\text{CO}_2$ instead.
subject: Chemistry

question: What is the effect of introducing an $\alpha$-halogen atom on the acidity of a carboxylic acid?
options: Acidity increases significantly due to the $-I$ (electron-withdrawing inductive) effect of the electronegative halogen
explanation: The strongly electronegative halogen stabilizes the carboxylate conjugate base via inductive electron withdrawal: bromoacetic acid ($pK_a \approx 2.90$) is much more acidic than acetic acid ($pK_a \approx 4.76$).
subject: Chemistry

question: Arrange the following in increasing order of acid strength: Acetic acid, Fluoroacetic acid, Chloroacetic acid, Bromoacetic acid:
explanation: Higher electronegativity of the $\alpha$-halogen exerts a stronger electron-withdrawing inductive ($-I$) effect, increasing acidity: $\text{F} > \text{Cl} > \text{Br} > \text{H}$.
subject: Chemistry

question: What is the product of the reaction: $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} \xrightarrow{\text{Br}_2 / \text{P}_{\text{red}}} A \xrightarrow{\text{KCN}} B \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+} C$?
explanation: Bromoacetic acid ($A$) reacts with cyanide to form cyanoacetic acid ($B$), which upon complete hydrolysis yields the dicarboxylic acid malonic acid ($C$).
subject: Chemistry

question: In the HVZ reaction, why is red phosphorus preferred over white phosphorus?
options: Red phosphorus is an acid while white phosphorus is a base
Red phosphorus is non-toxic, non-pyrophoric, and safe to handle, whereas white phosphorus is spontaneously flammable in air and highly toxic
White phosphorus does not react with halogens
explanation: Red phosphorus is stable at room temperature and allows controlled in situ generation of phosphorus halides without fire hazards.
subject: Chemistry

question: What happens when isobutyric acid ($(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCOOH}$) undergoes HVZ bromination?
options: No reaction occurs because it is hindered
explanation: Isobutyric acid has one $\alpha$-hydrogen on its tertiary carbon; bromination replaces this hydrogen selectively to give 2-bromo-2-methylpropanoic acid.
subject: Chemistry

question: Can a second bromine atom be introduced into isobutyric acid under HVZ conditions?
options: No, because the mono-brominated product has no remaining $\alpha$-hydrogens
explanation: Once the single $\alpha$-hydrogen of isobutyric acid is replaced, the resulting $\alpha$-bromo acid cannot enolize, terminating further halogenation.
subject: Chemistry

question: What is the product when butanoic acid is treated with $\text{Br}_2 / \text{P}_{\text{red}}$ followed by $\text{H}_2\text{O}$?
explanation: The HVZ reaction is strictly regiospecific for the $\alpha$-carbon, producing 2-bromobutanoic acid exclusively.
subject: Chemistry

question: Why does free molecular bromine NOT react directly with acetic acid in the absence of red phosphorus or acyl chloride?
options: Because carboxylic acids exist almost entirely in the keto/carboxyl form and have an extremely low, negligible equilibrium concentration of enol
Because acetic acid is a base
explanation: Unlike ketones, carboxylic acids have very low enol content ($K_{enol} < 10^{-12}$) due to resonance donation from the $-\text{OH}$ group; acyl halides enolize much faster.
subject: Chemistry

question: Instead of red phosphorus, which of the following reagents can be added in catalytic amounts to initiate the HVZ bromination?
explanation: Direct addition of catalytic $\text{PBr}_3$ or $\text{SOCl}_2$ generates the catalytic acyl halide in situ, bypassing the need for elemental phosphorus.
subject: Chemistry

question: What gas is continuously evolved during the HVZ bromination of carboxylic acids?
explanation: Halogenation of the enol generates one mole of hydrogen bromide gas: $\text{RCH}=\text{C(OH)X} + \text{X}_2 \rightarrow \text{RCH(X)COX} + \text{HX}\uparrow$.
subject: Chemistry

question: What is the product when 2-bromopropanoic acid is treated with excess ammonia?
explanation: Ammonolysis of 2-bromopropanoic acid substitutes the $\alpha$-bromine with an amino group, synthesizing the essential amino acid alanine.
subject: Chemistry

question: What is the synthesis sequence to convert acetic acid into glycine using HVZ reaction?
explanation: Chlorination of acetic acid gives chloroacetic acid, which on reaction with excess ammonia undergoes nucleophilic substitution to yield glycine.
subject: Chemistry

question: What is the IUPAC name of the product obtained when propanoic acid is subjected to HVZ reaction with bromine?
explanation: The bromine attaches at carbon-2 (the $\alpha$-carbon), yielding 2-bromopropanoic acid.
subject: Chemistry

question: Why does 2,2-dimethylpropanoic acid NOT react under HVZ conditions?
options: All four valencies of the $\alpha$-carbon are bonded to other carbons (three methyl groups), leaving zero $\alpha$-hydrogens
explanation: Pivalic acid ($(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-COOH}$) possesses a quaternary $\alpha$-carbon with no $\alpha$-hydrogens, completely preventing enolization.
subject: Chemistry

question: What is the stereochemical outcome when a racemic $\alpha$-bromo carboxylic acid is synthesized via HVZ reaction?
options: A racemic mixture ($\pm$) of enantiomers is formed because the planar achiral enol intermediate is attacked from either face with equal probability
A single pure optically active enantiomer
explanation: The enol intermediate is planar ($\,\text{sp}^2$ hybridized at the $\alpha$-carbon); halogen attacks from the top and bottom faces equally, producing a racemate.
subject: Chemistry

question: What happens when an $\alpha$-bromo acid is heated with zinc metal in ethanol?
options: Coupling to form a dicarboxylic acid
Debromination occurs via reduction back to the parent carboxylic acid ($R\text{CH(Br)COOH} \xrightarrow{\text{Zn/H}^+} R\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$)
explanation: Zinc in acid selectively reduces $\alpha$-halogen substituents, replacing the halogen with hydrogen to regenerate the unsubstituted carboxylic acid.
subject: Chemistry

question: Which of the following acids will undergo the HVZ reaction most rapidly?
options: Phenylacetic acid ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$, because the benzylic enol is resonance-stabilized by the aromatic ring)
explanation: Phenylacetic acid enolizes most readily because the resulting enol/enolate is conjugated with the aromatic $\pi$-system.

question: What is the product when adipic acid (hexanedioic acid) is treated with 2 equivalents of $\text{Br}_2 / \text{P}_{\text{red}}$ followed by $\text{H}_2\text{O}$?
explanation: Each of the two equivalent $\alpha$-carbons adjacent to the two carboxyl groups undergoes bromination, yielding 2,5-dibromohexanedioic acid.
subject: Chemistry

question: When 2,5-dibromohexanedioic acid is treated with base, what useful dicarboxylic acid is synthesized via double dehydrohalogenation?
explanation: Double elimination ($2 \times E2$) of $\text{HBr}$ from 2,5-dibromohexanedioic acid introduces two conjugated double bonds, yielding trans,trans-muconic acid.
subject: Chemistry

question: What is the product when 2-bromobutanoic acid is treated with potassium cyanide ($\text{KCN}$) followed by acid hydrolysis?
explanation: Cyanide displaces bromide via $S_N2$ to form 2-cyanobutanoic acid, which hydrolyzes to ethylmalonic acid.
subject: Chemistry

question: What is the purpose of adding water at the conclusion of the HVZ reaction?
options: To hydrolyze any remaining $\alpha$-halo acyl bromide and phosphorus halides back into carboxylic acids and phosphorous acid
explanation: The catalytic cycle generates $\alpha$-halo acyl bromide; water hydrolyzes this intermediate into the desired $\alpha$-halo carboxylic acid while destroying $\text{PBr}_3$.
subject: Chemistry

question: What happens if an alcohol ($R'\text{OH}$) is added instead of water during the workup of an HVZ reaction?
options: The alcohol oxidizes to an aldehyde
An $\alpha$-halo ester ($R\text{CH(Br)COOR}'$) is formed directly in high yield
explanation: The $\alpha$-halo acyl bromide reacts preferentially with the alcohol nucleophile, enabling one-pot synthesis of $\alpha$-halo esters.
subject: Chemistry

question: What is the product when propanoic acid is treated with $\text{Br}_2 / \text{P}_{\text{red}}$, followed by ethanol workup?
explanation: The intermediate 2-bromopropanoyl bromide reacts with ethanol to give ethyl 2-bromopropanoate directly.
subject: Chemistry

question: In the HVZ reaction, why does halogenation NOT occur at the $\beta$ or $\gamma$ carbons?
options: Because enolization involves ONLY the protons on the $\alpha$-carbon directly adjacent to the carbonyl group
Because the catalyst only binds to $\alpha$-carbons
explanation: Enol formation requires deprotonation at the carbon directly $\alpha$ to the carbonyl; carbons further away cannot form conjugated enols and remain unaffected.
subject: Chemistry

question: What is the oxidation state of phosphorus in $\text{PBr}_3$?
explanation: Phosphorus is bonded to three electronegative bromine atoms ($-1$ each), giving phosphorus an oxidation state of $+3$.
subject: Chemistry

question: What is the major inorganic byproduct obtained during the water quenching of an HVZ reaction using $\text{P}_{\text{red}}$?
explanation: Hydrolysis of phosphorus tribromide yields phosphorous acid: $\text{PBr}_3 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{H}_3\text{PO}_3 + 3\text{HBr}$.
subject: Chemistry

question: Which of the following compounds will give a positive HVZ reaction?
options: Cyclohexanecarboxylic acid (has one $\alpha$-hydrogen at the ring junction)
explanation: Cyclohexanecarboxylic acid has a single $\alpha$-hydrogen on C-1 of the ring, which is replaced by bromine to give 1-bromocyclohexanecarboxylic acid.
subject: Chemistry

question: What is the product of: $\text{Cyclohexanecarboxylic acid} \xrightarrow{\text{Br}_2 / \text{P}_{\text{red}}} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_2\text{O}} X$?
explanation: Bromination occurs selectively at the $\alpha$-methine carbon (C-1) of the cyclohexane ring.
subject: Chemistry

question: Identify the reagent $Y$ in: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(Br)COOH} \xrightarrow{Y} \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)COOH}$:
explanation: Aqueous hydroxide or moist silver oxide provides nucleophilic substitution of bromide without causing dehydrohalogenation elimination.

question: What is the relative rate of bromination of acyl bromide compared to the parent carboxylic acid?
options: Both react at the exact same rate
Acyl bromide enolizes and reacts over $10^5$ times faster than the carboxylic acid
explanation: The electron-withdrawing bromine atom on the carbonyl accelerates enol formation dramatically compared to the electron-donating $-\text{OH}$ group of the carboxylic acid.
subject: Chemistry

question: What is the ultimate synthetic significance of the HVZ reaction in organic chemistry?
options: It provides an indispensable, regioselective pathway to convert readily available aliphatic carboxylic acids into $\alpha$-amino acids, $\alpha$-hydroxy acids, and $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated acids
It is used to synthesize long-chain alkanes
It provides a route to aromatic rings from methane
It is used to crack petroleum
explanation: The introduction of an $\alpha$-halogen unlocks versatile nucleophilic substitutions and eliminations to synthesize pharmaceuticals, amino acids, and polymer monomers.
